sections.title: The questions serious buyers ask before committing
sections.description: No vague promises and no hidden discovery call required to understand the fundamentals.

items.objection: How much will an LLM project cost?
items.answer: Focused integrations typically range from $20,000 to $50,000, RAG systems from $20,000 to $80,000, and agentic or enterprise platforms from $40,000 upward. Your agreement contains a fixed quote based on the approved scope.

Most single-use-case integrations and RAG systems require 6–14 weeks. Agentic workflows commonly require 12–22 weeks because tool permissions, recovery behavior and approval logic demand deeper engineering.
We combine retrieval grounding, source citations, confidence thresholds, structured output validation, human escalation and quantitative evaluation appropriate to the risk level of your use case.

items.objection: Can you meet compliance and data-residency requirements?
items.answer: Yes. Compliance requirements influence the architecture from discovery. Options include controlled third-party APIs, regional cloud deployment and fully self-hosted Llama or Mistral infrastructure.

sections.title: RAG quality is determined by architecture—not by adding a vector database
sections.description: Reliable retrieval requires deliberate decisions across document preparation, search, ranking, context construction and evaluation.

blocks.heading: Semantic and structure-aware chunking
paragraphs: Naive fixed-length chunking frequently separates a coherent idea across multiple chunks. We split content around semantic and structural boundaries so retrieved passages preserve the context required to answer accurately.
bullets: Configurable overlap based on document type

blocks.heading: Hybrid retrieval
paragraphs: Embedding search understands concepts but may miss exact part numbers, clauses or error codes. Hybrid retrieval combines semantic search with keyword search and fuses the results to improve both conceptual and exact-match recall.

blocks.heading: Re-ranking
paragraphs: Initial retrieval produces candidate passages. A re-ranking layer scores those candidates against the user query before the final context is passed to the generation model, improving relevance and reducing noise.

blocks.heading: Evaluation-driven iteration
paragraphs: We create representative queries with known supporting sources and measure retrieval precision and recall throughout development. This exposes systematic gaps that subjective answer review normally misses.

sections.title: Fine-tuning is powerful when the economics and data support it

blocks.heading: When fine-tuning is worthwhile
paragraphs: Fine-tuning makes sense for a narrow and repeated task where prompting plus RAG has already been tested and still fails to achieve the required accuracy or consistency.

blocks.heading: When fine-tuning is the wrong tool
paragraphs: General knowledge questions, rapidly changing source information and small low-quality datasets are usually better handled with prompting, retrieval or application-level logic.
bullets: Fewer than several hundred quality examples
Problems already solved reliably with RAG

sections.title: Agentic systems that act with explicit boundaries
sections.description: Production agents need more than tool calling. They require permissions, durable state, recovery behavior and human control wherever an action has real-world consequences.

items.title: Bounded Tool Access
items.description: Every agent receives access only to explicitly approved tools and actions rather than unrestricted production access.

items.title: Durable Checkpoints
items.description: Long-running workflows persist progress and can recover from a failure point without restarting the entire task.

items.title: Human Approval Gates
items.description: Financial transactions, external messages, destructive changes and other sensitive actions pause for authorized approval.

sections.title: Control inference cost before usage becomes expensive
sections.description: Cost architecture is designed during development instead of being added after monthly API usage becomes a problem.

items.title: Model Routing
items.description: Simple classification and extraction tasks route to smaller models while complex reasoning uses a more capable model.

items.title: Semantic Caching
items.description: Repeated or semantically similar requests reuse verified responses when appropriate, reducing cost and improving latency.

items.title: Context Optimization
items.description: Retrieval count, prompt structure and supplied context are optimized so every request uses only the tokens required for a reliable response.

items.title: Batch Processing
items.description: Non-real-time document processing and classification workloads use batch execution where lower-cost provider options are available.

items.question: What is the difference between LLM integration and fine-tuning?
items.answer: LLM integration uses an existing foundation model through an API or self-hosted endpoint with prompting and often RAG. Fine-tuning changes model weights using domain examples to improve narrow repeated tasks. Most business use cases should test integration plus RAG before investing in fine-tuning.

items.question: Which model should we use: GPT-4, Claude, Gemini, Llama or Mistral?
items.answer: The correct model depends on your task, expected volume, accuracy requirements, context size, latency target, cloud environment and data-governance constraints. ClickMasters evaluates candidate models against representative tasks instead of defaulting to one provider.

items.question: Can we self-host an open-weight model?
items.answer: Yes. Llama and Mistral can be deployed on infrastructure you control. Self-hosting offers stronger data control and can reduce marginal cost at high usage, but it introduces GPU infrastructure and model-serving responsibilities.

items.question: How do you prevent company-specific hallucinations?
items.answer: The primary technique is RAG grounding against your current knowledge base. Depending on risk, we also implement citations, confidence thresholds, structured output validation, human escalation and evaluation suites.

items.question: Do you develop AI agents that can take actions?
items.answer: Yes. We build multi-step agents that call approved tools and APIs. Sensitive actions use permission boundaries, checkpoints, audit logs and human approval gates rather than unlimited autonomy.

items.question: How is an LLM development project priced?
items.answer: Development is delivered as a fixed-price project based on an approved scope. Ongoing API usage or self-hosting infrastructure is billed separately and is not hidden inside the development fee.

items.question: What happens to our data when using a third-party model API?
items.answer: Enterprise API configurations are selected to prevent submitted data from being used for provider model training where supported. When data cannot leave your controlled environment, we can design a self-hosted open-weight deployment.

items.question: How do you measure whether the system works?
items.answer: We use task-specific evaluation: retrieval precision and recall for RAG, labeled task accuracy, hallucination rate, output validity, latency and cost. These benchmarks are established before launch and retained for regression testing.

items.question: How long does a RAG system remain accurate?
items.answer: A RAG system retrieves from the live knowledge base, so it does not become stale like model training data. Its accuracy depends on keeping source documents current and automatically synchronizing document changes into the retrieval index.

items.question: Can you migrate an existing integration between model providers?
items.answer: Yes. Provider-agnostic architecture can reduce migration cost, but prompts, evaluation and behavior still need to be re-tested because models interpret instructions differently.

items.question: What happens when a foundation-model provider updates its model?
items.answer: Regression tests run against the established evaluation set so behavioral changes can be detected before they affect production users. Model and prompt versions should be tracked as controlled dependencies.

items.question: Will we receive the source code and intellectual property?
items.answer: Yes. ClickMasters projects include full ownership of the custom source code and project IP defined in the agreement.

sections.title: Questions that reveal whether an LLM vendor has shipped real production systems

blocks.heading: Ask for architecture, not reassurance
paragraphs: Ask the vendor to explain how hallucination would be reduced for your specific use case. A credible answer should cover grounding, retrieval quality, confidence behavior, evaluation and escalation—not simply claim that the model is highly accurate.

blocks.heading: Ask how fine-tuning decisions are made
paragraphs: A trustworthy vendor should be willing to recommend prompting or RAG when those approaches solve the problem more economically than fine-tuning.

blocks.heading: Ask for concrete evaluation methodology
paragraphs: Request details about test-set construction, task metrics, retrieval precision, hallucination measurement and regression testing. Production quality cannot be established through a handful of impressive demonstrations.

blocks.heading: Ask what happens after a production failure
paragraphs: Experienced teams can explain how provider updates, retrieval degradation, tool failures and unexpected outputs are detected, contained and investigated.

sections.heading: Turn your LLM idea into a production architecture
sections.text: Bring us the task, the available data and your governance constraints. We will help determine whether your project needs integration, RAG, fine-tuning, an agentic workflow or a self-hosted model.
